Timeline::isoformat¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline::isoformat() -> std::string

Formats one scalar timestamp into canonical ISO-style text.

This is the scalar convenience surface for the common question: “give me the machine-readable text for this one moment”.

Unlike strftime(...), isoformat() does not ask you to supply a format pattern. Unlike to_note_iso(), it is not the vectorized text-export surface for a full timeline.

Parameters¶

This method takes no parameters.

The main usage choice is about the shape of the source object:

  • use isoformat() for a scalar Timeline

  • use to_note_iso() for 1D or higher-rank timelines

Returns¶

std::string Canonical ISO-style timestamp text with explicit offset and fractional second precision.

Notes¶

  • isoformat() is the right surface for logs, keys, diagnostics, and scalar serialization.

  • The output is stable and explicit: the verified example includes full nanosecond precision and a +00:00 offset.

  • If you are formatting many timestamps at once, to_note_iso() is usually the more natural API.

Examples¶

Example 1. Format one scalar timestamp into canonical text.

auto text = scalar.isoformat();
std::cout << text << "\n";

Output¶

2024-11-01T09:00:00.000000000+00:00

Example 2. When the source is not scalar, switch to the vectorized ISO conversion surface instead of forcing isoformat().

auto labels = with_nat.to_note_iso();
std::cout << pluss::note::print(labels) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["2024-11-01T09:00:00.000000000+00:00", "NaT", "2024-12-31T23:59:59.000000000+00:00", "NaT"]
